Required and optional fields

An interface or type alias can describe an object’s fields. A trailing question mark marks a field as optional. With strict null checks, handle the missing value before you use it as a string.

interface Product {
  name: string;
  price: number;
  label?: string;
}

function displayName(product: Product) {
  return product.label ?? product.name;
}

Narrow with a check

Use typeof, equality, or a shared literal field to narrow a union. In the example, checking ok lets the compiler determine which fields exist in each branch.

type Result =
  | { ok: true; total: number }
  | { ok: false; message: string };

function describe(result: Result) {
  if (result.ok) return "Total: " + result.total;
  return result.message;
}
